title: Functional user tests — every admin data grid actually draws
notes:
Intent-level steps, no selectors: selectors churn, intent does not. The probe resolves controls from the accessibility tree. 'verified' records the last real browser run.

Why this suite exists: on 2026-10-25 three core grids were serving HTTP 200 with an empty table and zero console errors, because their controller never set useDataTables and each grid script opens with a bail-out guard (TIGER-390). Nothing in PHPUnit renders a page, and the browser probe's cheapest detector is 'no console errors' — which a working guard defeats. So a grid has to be LOOKED AT.

The hard-won rule here is UI-GRID-EMPTY-TRUTH: an empty grid and a broken grid are the same picture. Never record a PASS on an empty grid without establishing WHY it is empty. Run `tests/ui/bin/seed-dev.php` first so the org-scoped grids are supposed to have rows.

steps: open each admin screen that renders a data grid
check the page actually loaded jQuery, DataTables and tiger.datatable.js
expect: the screen's controller set useDataTables, so the admin layout emitted the grid libs
the `tigerDataTable` global is defined before the screen's own JS runs
no screen relies on another page having loaded the lib
scenarios.verified: 2026-10-25 PASS — all 14 reachable grid screens serve dataTables.min.js; /comment/admin 404s only because comments are disabled, which is correct. `paradigm-scan.php` now covers this statically (check 5, datatable_gate), so it should never need finding by hand again.

steps: wait for the grid to settle past its Loading… state
read the row count and the 'Showing x to y of z' summary
expect: sortable column headers, a search box and pagination are present (the lib initialised)
scenarios.verified: 2026-10-25 PASS — /access/user 25 of 29 · /access/org 25 of 27 · /cms/page 25 of 25 · /system/updates 24 · /email/admin 5 of 5 · /agent/skills 25 of 133 · /translations 25 of 2,597 · /system/modules 25 · /blog/post 1 of 1 · /cms/menu 1 of 1 · /code 1 of 1 · /newsletter/admin 1 of 1. Zero console errors across the pass.

steps: note every grid that reports zero rows
for each, establish from the data WHY it is empty — no rows anywhere, or none in this caller's scope
expect: an empty grid is never recorded as PASS on the strength of the empty state alone
a grid whose table is genuinely empty shows the grid's own empty message, not a dead table
if rows exist and are not drawn, that is a defect
scenarios.verified: 2026-10-25 PASS — /media is correctly empty (10 media rows exist, all owned by other orgs; Tiger_Model_Media::datatable scopes to the caller's org OR the shared '' library). /system/sites is correctly empty (no host->org mappings on dev). This check is the one that caught TIGER-391: /cms/page's 25 rows looked like a healthy grid next to media's honest 0, which is what exposed the missing org filter.

steps: open a grid screen whose /api call fails, or misconfigure one on purpose
watch for a native browser dialog
expect: no alert/confirm/prompt ever — the house rule holds for third-party libs too
a grid error reaches the CONSOLE, where the probe can see it
a grid missing {module, service, action} is refused at the call site with the cause named
scenarios.verified: 2026-10-25 PASS — DataTables' default errMode is alert(), which both broke the rule and HID a server-side TypeError behind a modal. tiger.datatable.js now sets errMode='throw' and guards the service descriptor; mutation-checked in-page by re-passing the old `method:` shape — returns null and logs "use `action`, not `method`" with no dialog.

scenarios.role: superadmin of an org that owns no content
steps: sign in as an admin whose org owns no pages and no media
open the Content grid and the Media grid
compare what each one lists against what the signed-in org actually owns
take a page_id belonging to ANOTHER org and open it directly in the editor
expect: a grid lists only the caller's own org plus genuinely shared ('' org) rows
a cross-org id is refused, not loaded into the editor
an admin widens scope by OPTING IN, never by default
scenarios.verified: 2026-10-25 FAIL — TIGER-391. /cms/page listed all 25 pages across three orgs to a superadmin whose org owns none, and /cms/page/edit/id/<another org's page> loaded title, slug and a 703-char body. /media behaved correctly on the same account (0 rows), which is what made the contrast visible. The save/delete path reads as unscoped too, but was NOT exercised — proving it means mutating another org's content.
